hypothesis: A unique submission raster can be built under the current 13GEMSDOE lattice duplicate-stop by placing dots only where the lattice has no cover: all 6,649 valid cells farther than 3 px from any lattice dot, plus 13,351 dots inside the lattice neighbourhood but outside the stopped CTD-1/FC-1 3 px neighbourhoods (20,000 dots total; 66.76% within 3 px of lattice dots, below the 70% stop). On the catalogue-proxy holdout it should show distance-weighted Tversky skill above a count-matched random-dots control.
mechanism: Sparse binary dots (value 1.0) on geometrically selected cells, 0.0 elsewhere inside the footprint, NaN outside; no catalogue-derived features, no labels used in placement, no model fitting. The dot locations are the entire signal; the metric rewards dots landing within 300 m of hidden new-fault pixels and penalises dots near mapped faults.
named_non_fault_process: Erosional scarps, lava-flow fronts, lithologic boundaries and survey/flight-line artifacts can produce line-like or clustered geophysical/topographic evidence that a dot-based raster would credit even though no concealed fault exists.
